title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events — what you did, where you went, what happened — using the simple past and the ने construction.
intro:
Time to tell people what you did at the weekend, where you went on holiday, or what went wrong.

The Hindi past tense has one famous feature: the **ने construction**. With most verbs that take an object (eat, see, do, buy), the subject gets the little word **ने** and the verb agrees with the **object**, not the subject. It sounds strange at first — **मैंने चाय पी** 'I drank tea', where पी is feminine because चाय is — but after a few dozen sentences it becomes natural.

grammar.title: The simple past (intransitive verbs)
grammar.body:
The simple past is the **past participle**: verb stem + an ending that agrees like an adjective:

**-ā** m. sg · **-e** m. pl / आप / तुम · **-ī** f. sg · **-īṃ** f. pl

बैठना → बैठा, बैठे, बैठी, बैठीं. If the stem ends in a vowel, a y is added in the masculine: आना → **आया**, आए, आई, आईं; सोना → **सोया**.

Irregular: **जाना → गया** (गए, गई, गईं) · **होना → हुआ** (हुए, हुई, हुईं) · **करना → किया** · **देना → दिया** · **लेना → लिया** · **पीना → पिया**.

With **intransitive** verbs (no object: go, come, sit, sleep, arrive…) the verb simply agrees with the subject: **मैं गया** (m) / **मैं गई** (f), **वे आए**.

Note: in conversation people very often add था: **मैं बाज़ार गया था** — this is the normal way to describe a completed past event, especially one that's no longer relevant now.

examples.native: मैं रात को देर से सोई।
examples.roman: maiṃ rāt ko der se soī.
examples.en: I went to sleep late last night. (woman)

grammar.title: The ने construction (transitive verbs)
grammar.body:
With **transitive** verbs (eat, drink, see, do, buy, say…) in the past, three things happen:

**1.** The subject takes **ने**: मैं → **मैंने**, तू → तूने, वह → **उसने**, यह → इसने, हम → **हमने**, तुम → **तुमने**, आप → **आपने**, वे → **उन्होंने**, ये → इन्होंने. Nouns go oblique: लड़का → लड़के ने.

**2.** The verb agrees with the **object**: मैंने **चाय** पी (चाय f) · मैंने **खाना** खाया (m) · मैंने दो **फ़िल्में** देखीं (f. pl).

**3.** If the object has **को** (usually a specific person), the verb goes to the default **masculine singular**: मैंने **उसको** देखा 'I saw him/her' — even if 'her'.

So **राम ने रोटी खाई** 'Ram ate a roti' and **सीता ने आम खाया** 'Sita ate a mango' — the verb looks at what was eaten, not who ate.

A few common verbs **don't** take ने even though they have objects: **लाना** 'bring', **भूलना** 'forget', **बोलना** 'speak' (usually). And all **intransitive** verbs never take ने.

examples.en: I drank tea. (पी: चाय is f)
They / he (resp.) didn't say anything to me.

examples.native: मैंने प्रिया को बाज़ार में देखा।
examples.roman: maiṃne Priyā ko bāzār meṃ dekhā.
examples.en: I saw Priya in the market. (को → default देखा)

grammar.title: था and 'was doing'
grammar.body:
The past of **होना** 'to be' agrees like an adjective: **था** (m. sg), **थे** (m. pl / आप / तुम), **थी** (f. sg), **थीं** (f. pl). मैं बीमार था 'I was ill', वे घर पर थीं 'they (f) were at home'.

Put था in place of है in the present tenses to move them into the past:

**Past continuous**: मैं सो **रहा था** 'I was sleeping'
**Past habitual**: मैं वहाँ काम **करता था** 'I used to work there'

These never take ने, whatever the verb: **मैं खाना खा रहा था** 'I was eating'.

examples.en: The weather was very nice yesterday.

examples.native: जब तुमने फ़ोन किया, मैं नहा रही थी।
examples.roman: jab tumne fon kiyā, maiṃ nahā rahī thī.
examples.en: When you called, I was in the shower. (woman)

examples.native: बचपन में हम गाँव में रहते थे।
examples.roman: bachpan meṃ ham gāṃv meṃ rahte the.
examples.en: As children we used to live in a village.

examples.native: बच्चे पार्क में खेल रहे थे।

examples.en: The children were playing in the park.

dialogue.title: How was your weekend?
dialogue.setting: Monday morning at the office. Nisha asks her colleague David about his weekend.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: गुड मॉर्निंग, डेविड! वीकेंड कैसा रहा? आपने क्या किया?
lines.roman: guḍ morniṅg, Ḍeviḍ! vīkeṇḍ kaisā rahā? āpne kyā kiyā?
lines.en: Good morning, David! How was the weekend? What did you do?

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: शनिवार को मैं दोस्तों के साथ आगरा गया।
lines.roman: shanivār ko maiṃ dostoṃ ke sāth Āgrā gayā.
lines.en: On Saturday I went to Agra with friends.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: अरे वाह! आपने ताज महल देखा?
lines.roman: are vāh! āpne Tāj Mahal dekhā?
lines.en: Oh wow! Did you see the Taj Mahal?

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: हाँ, हम सुबह छह बजे पहुँचे। बहुत सुंदर था!
lines.roman: hāṃ, ham subah chhah baje pahuṃche. bahut sundar thā!
lines.en: Yes, we got there at six in the morning. It was beautiful!

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: हमने पेठा ख़रीदा और एक ढाबे पर खाना खाया। पर फिर एक गड़बड़ हो गई…
lines.roman: hamne peṭhā xarīdā aur ek ḍhābe par khānā khāyā. par phir ek gaṛbaṛ ho gaī…
lines.en: We bought petha and ate at a dhaba. But then something went wrong…

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: वापसी में मेरा फ़ोन खो गया! शायद ट्रेन में गिर गया।
lines.roman: vāpsī meṃ merā fon kho gayā! shāyad ṭren meṃ gir gayā.
lines.en: On the way back I lost my phone! Maybe it fell out on the train.

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: अरे नहीं! फिर आपने क्या किया?
lines.roman: are nahīṃ! phir āpne kyā kiyā?
lines.en: Oh no! What did you do then?

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: मेरे दोस्त ने मेरे नंबर पर फ़ोन किया, और एक अंकल ने उठाया।
lines.roman: mere dost ne mere nambar par fon kiyā, aur ek aṅkal ne uṭhāyā.
lines.en: My friend called it, and an older man picked up.

lines.speaker: David
lines.native: उन्होंने कल शाम को मेरा फ़ोन वापस भेजा!
lines.roman: unhoṃne kal shām ko merā fon vāpas bhejā!
lines.en: He sent my phone back yesterday evening!

lines.speaker: Nisha
lines.native: बहुत अच्छे लोग थे! आपकी क़िस्मत अच्छी है।
lines.roman: bahut achchhe log the! āpkī qismat achchhī hai.

culture: **आपने खाना खाया?** 'Have you eaten?' is a common, caring question from elders and hosts — say हाँ, खा लिया even if you just had a snack, or expect to be fed! When telling stories, Hindi speakers often switch into the present tense for drama, and use lots of **फिर** 'then' and **तो** 'so'. Note how David refers to the helpful stranger with the respectful plural (उन्होंने) — older people you don't know are always spoken about respectfully, even behind their backs.

lessons.title: Where did you go?

tip.title: मैं गया, मैं गई — went
tip.body:
- The simple past changes like an adjective: **-आ** (m), **-ई** (f), **-ए** (pl / आप / तुम): मैं आया, मैं आई, हम आए.
- Irregular: जाना → **गया / गई / गए**, होना → **हुआ / हुई / हुए**.
- Verbs with no object (go, come, arrive, sleep) just agree with the subject.
- Adding **था** is very common for a finished event: मैं दिल्ली गया **था**.
tip.pattern: मैं गया (m)  ·  मैं गई (f)  ·  हम गए

tip.title: मैंने चाय पी — the ने past
tip.body:
- With verbs that take an object (eat, see, do, buy, say), the doer takes **ने**: मैं → **मैंने**, वह → **उसने**, आप → **आपने**, हम → **हमने**.
- The verb agrees with the **thing**, not the person: मैंने चाय **पी** (f), मैंने खाना **खाया** (m).
- With **को** on a person, it stays **-आ**: मैंने उसको **देखा**.
- Irregular: करना → **किया**, लेना → **लिया**.
tip.pattern: मैंने + object + verb (agrees with the object)

sentences.en: What did you say to him?
I saw her at the party.

lessons.title: Lost, broken, forgotten

tip.title: It broke vs. I broke it
tip.body:
- Things that happen *by themselves* use **गया** and no ने: फ़ोन **खो गया** 'the phone got lost', गिलास **टूट गया** 'the glass broke', मैं **भूल गया** 'I forgot'.
- If someone *did* it, use the ने past: **किसने** तोड़ा? 'who broke it?'
- **लाना** 'bring' never takes ने: वह फूल **लाया**.

sentences.en: My phone fell, but it didn't break.

lessons.title: When I was little

tip.title: था — was, used to
tip.body:
- **था** 'was' agrees: **था** (m), **थी** (f), **थे** (pl / आप), **थीं** (f pl).
- 'Was doing': मैं सो **रहा था** 'I was sleeping'.
- 'Used to': बचपन में मैं क्रिकेट **खेलता था**.
- These never take ने.
tip.pattern: verb + रहा था (was doing)  ·  verb-ता था (used to)
